name: data_summary.txt
text:
*******************************************************************************
** Data summary for: Data for Advanced Metrology Suite for Linking Residual  **
** Stress to Fundamental Properties of Thermoset Packaging Materials         **
*******************************************************************************

Authors: Polette Centellas, Stian Romberg, Ran Tao, Alexander K Landauer

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA SOURCES (top level folders):
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DIC_data: Data for the digital image correlation (DIC) experiment, including 
          example raw data (images), setup information and metadata in their 
		  native format and as .csv or .txt files, and processed results (.mat). 
		  The figure is included as a .png.

DSC_data: Reduced data in .xlsx files from DSC experiments used to generate 
          figures for the associated ECTC manuscript and the resultant figures 
		  in .qpc and .tif formats.
                    
Rheology_data: Reduced data from a parallel plate separate actuator-transducer 
               rheometer in the form of .csv files used to generate figures.

Stress_bench_data: Data from a stress bench setup equipped with a multi-beam 
                   optical stress sensor that monitors changes in the thin film 
				   curvature during thermal cycling experiments, similar 
				   measurements where the curvature is measured during the 
				   curing process, and water vapor sorption-desorption 
				   experiments. Reduced data are included in .csv and .xlsx 
				   files, with the resultant figures as .png images.




-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MATERIAL TESTED:
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

EW8002 "NoSWEEP" Wire Bond Encapsulant: Low viscosity thermal cure epoxy with 
high degree of filler and dyed with carbon black for laser etchablity.
Manufacture quoted typical specifications are as follows:
_______________________________________________________________________________
UNCURED (WET) PROPERTIES
Color: Black
Filler Content Filler avg size/max 6/30 microns: 70 %
Viscosity @ 25ºC RVDV-II+ , Spindle 14, Cup 6R: 50 kcps @ 0.5 rpm
Pot Life @ 25º C: > 24 hours
Density: 1.7 gram/cm3
_______________________________________________________________________________
PROCESS PARAMETERS
Cure Cycle
60 min @ 100 ºC + 60 min @ 165 ºC
Alternate Cure Cycle
30 min @ 100 ºC + 120 min @ 150 ºC
_______________________________________________________________________________
CURED PROPERTIES
Glass Transition Temp. (Tg) by DMA: 150 ºC
Coefficient of Thermal Expansion (CTE): 15 ppm/ºC
Flexural Modulus (Three Point Bend): 2.0 GPa @ 25 ºC
Extractable Ionic Content:
   Cl < 10
   K < 5
   Na < 10
   F < 5

   
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DISCLAIMER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Certain commercial equipment, instruments, or materials are identified in this 
dataset in order to specify the experimental procedure adequately.  Such 
identification is not intended to imply recommendation or endorsement by NIST, 
nor is it intended to imply that the materials or equipment identified are 
necessarily the best available for the purpose.

name: DSC_data/DSC_data_notes.txt
text:
Notes on the differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) measurements:

All measurements are performed by Ran Tao using a TA Instruments Discovery 
DSC 2500 equipped with a refrigerated cooling system under nitrogen. About 
10 mg to 15 mg of uncured encapsulant samples are sealed in 40 µL hermetic 
pans for measurement.

The standard uncertainties for temperature and heat flow are approximately 
± 1 % and ± 3 %, respectively.

Model-based kinetics analysis and simulation are performed using NETZSCH 
Kinetics Neo software.

name: Rheology_data/rheology_data_notes.txt
text:
Notes on the rheology measurements:

All measurements are performed by Stian Romberg using a TA Instruments ARES-G2
equipped with a parallel plate fixture using optimally windowed chirps (OWCh)
method. The instrument has a minimum resolvable torque of ± 0.05 μN.m and 
angle of ± 0.04 μrad.

We identify the critical strain below which the viscoelastic moduli are strain-
independent, i.e., the linear viscoelastic region, by conducting amplitude sweep 
experiments where strain amplitude, g, is varied from 10^-1 % strain to 10^2 % strain 
at isothermal  temperatures. The critical strain is temperature-dependent, with the 
lowest value (g about 0.3 % strain) occurring at the maximum temperature tested of 
100 °C. Therefore, we maintain the strain amplitude well below this critical value 
in consecutive experiments to measure the linear viscoelastic moduli. 

The uncertainty of each measurement is at most ± 7 %, except between 70 °C and 80 °C 
where G" reaches a minimum and uncertainty is at most ± 20 %. 

Complete test methods and raw data are available upon reasonable request.

name: Stress_bench_data/Stress_data_notes.txt
text:
Notes on the thin film curvature/stress measurements:

Thin film measurements are performed by Polette Centellas and Gery Stafford 
using a stress bench setup equipped with a multi-beam optical stress sensor 
that monitors changes in the thin film curvature during thermal cycling 
experiments. The thin film sample is cycled between 35 °C and 65 °C for at 
least 10 heat-cool cycles. The curvature resolution is typically 
2 × 10E-4 1/m, or 5 km radius of curvature. The film stress is calculated 
from the thin film curvature according to Stoney’s formula for an arbitrary 
thickness and modulus ratio between the film and substrate. 

Similar film curvature measurements are performed by Karl F. Schoch, Jr. In 
these experiments, the curvature is measured during the curing process (60 min 
at 100 °C followed by 60 min at 165 °C). Once the curing schedule is completed, 
the film is cooled back to room temperature and then cycled to 150 °C for three 
heat-cool cycles. The film is left for 1 month at ambient conditions, and then 
heat-cooled for two cycles between 25 °C and 200 °C.  

Water vapor sorption-desorption experiments are performed by Huong Giang Nguyen 
using a VTI-SA+ automated vapor sorption analyzer (TA Instruments, USA) at 
ambient pressure and with nitrogen (99.999 % purity) as the carrier gas. The 
desired percent relative humidity (% RH) is obtained by continuously mixing a 
dry nitrogen flow with a humid nitrogen flow. The instrument has a ± 0.1 μg 
mass resolution and a ± 1 % RH control standard uncertainty based on 
manufacturer specifications. A small sample is first conditioned for 6 h at
65 °C under pure nitrogen flow (0 % RH). For sorption experiments, the 
sample environment is then set to 60 % RH for approximately 10 h at an 
isothermal temperature (25 °C and 50 °C). Then, the sample environment is set 
to 2 % RH for approximately 6 h at the same isothermal temperature to 
investigate the desorption behavior. Mass changes during the experiments 
are calculated relative to the dry mass measured at the end of the conditioning
stage.  

Complete test methods and raw data are available upon reasonable request.

name: DIC_data/DIC_data_notes.txt
text:
Notes on the stereo digital image correlation (DIC) measurements:

All measurements are performed by Alexander Landauer using a pair of 24.4 MPx 
cameras (ace2 a2A5328-15umPRO Monochrome, Basler AG) with 50 mm lenses (Fujinon 
CF50ZA-1S, Fujifilm Corp.) in a custom environmental chamber (based on a GF-C2 
oven from DDM Novastar, Ivyland, PA) with a large antireflective coated
window (approximately 300 mm square) and 3 LED light panels for illumination.
A roughly circular epoxy blob (approximately 600 mg to 800 mg) was allowed to 
self-level on a flexible backer before being speckled with white spray paint.

The customary DIC parameter table is as follows:

|-----------------------------------------------------------|
|    Parameter [unit]             Value                     |
|-----------------------------------------------------------|
 Region of Interest (ROI) [px]    Approx. 910 × 895    
 Aperture                         f/16    
 Image scale [µm/px]              1.23    
 Stereo angle [°]                 -18.2    
 Stand-off distance [mm]          241 mm    
 Exposure time [ms]               19    
 Image filtering                  Gaussian 5 px kernel    
 Reference image                  Cumulative with update 
                                  for iteration > 6    
 Interpolation                    Bi-cubic spline    
 Matching criterion               Zero-normalized sum-of-
                                  square differences with 
								  Gaussian weighting    
 Subset size [px]                 41    
 Step size [px]                   19    
 Subset shape function            Affine    
 Strain Window                    21
 Virtual strain gauge [px]        421    
 Strain formulation               Green-Lagrange with Q4 
                                  interpolant    
 Static noise floor [µm/m]        22.4    
|-----------------------------------------------------------|

Stereo-DIC analysis was conducting using MatchID-Stereo in accordance with 
the International Digital Image Correlation Society’s Good Practices Guide.
